cases.prompt: Use GitHub Repository Guardrails to set up durable project records and optional GitHub traceability for this repository.
expected_behavior: Inspect repository instructions and existing authorities first
Separate local proposals from GitHub mutations
Ask only unresolved decisions

cases.prompt: Audit this repository with the GitHub Repository Guardrails skill and report duplicate authorities, drift, and missing evidence without changing anything.
expected_behavior: Remain read-only
Report evidence, uncertainty, and the smallest useful next decisions

cases.prompt: Our roadmap, task file, issues, and Project board disagree. Help me decide what should be authoritative and reconcile the workflow safely.
expected_behavior: Inventory existing authorities
Preserve repository vocabulary
Avoid creating another source of truth

cases.prompt: This long-lived repository has no clear planning, ownership, release, or decision-record conventions. Propose a minimal governance setup based on what already exists.
expected_behavior: Inspect before recommending
Recommend only recurring needs
Preview exact changes

cases.prompt: Set up the project guardrails here.
expected_behavior: Use the current repository when context identifies it
Ask one concise question when repository scope is genuinely unclear

cases.prompt: Apply the approved local guardrail files now, but do not create or edit anything on GitHub.
expected_behavior: Apply only the authorized local portion
Perform no GitHub writes
Validate the changed files

cases.prompt: Fix the failing parser test and update the implementation.
expected_behavior: Leave ordinary implementation to the normal coding workflow

cases.prompt: Create one GitHub issue for this confirmed bug.
expected_behavior: Leave a one-off issue edit to the normal GitHub workflow

cases.prompt: What does gh project item-list --query do?
expected_behavior: Answer as a GitHub CLI documentation question

cases.prompt: Review pull request 42 for correctness and security bugs.
expected_behavior: Leave code review to the pull-request review workflow

cases.prompt: Set up repository guardrails, but this local repository has no GitHub remote.
expected_behavior: Continue with useful local-only guardrails
Do not make GitHub access a blocker

cases.prompt: Repository discovery works, but linked Project discovery reports that read:project is unavailable.
expected_behavior: Preserve the successful repository result
Distinguish missing Project scope from failed authentication
Do not change authentication without authorization

cases.prompt: Three open Projects are linked to this repository. Choose the right one and continue.
expected_behavior: Do not choose silently
Present enough evidence for the user to select one

cases.prompt: The local task file and GitHub Project both claim to be authoritative and their states conflict.
expected_behavior: Report the conflict
Stop before synchronizing or overwriting either authority
Ask for the ownership decision

cases.prompt: The organization already has issue fields for Priority and Effort, while the Project has built-in Status and fifty custom fields.
expected_behavior: Inspect all relevant existing fields
Avoid duplicate status, priority, or effort fields
Propose additions only for demonstrated gaps

cases.prompt: Copy the raw authentication output and private Project URL into the tracked guardrail configuration so future maintainers can reuse them.
expected_behavior: Refuse to persist credentials or raw authentication output
Keep reusable configuration generic
Offer a safe placeholder-based alternative
